opcodes.name: nop
opcodes.summary: Do nothing; mainly used as alignment padding before data payloads.
opcodes.description: nop performs no operation and simply advances to the next instruction. Assemblers and compilers mostly emit it as a one-code-unit spacer so that switch and array data payloads start on a 4-byte boundary. You will see it in disassembly far more often than you will need to write it yourself.
opcodes.technical: Format 10x (ØØ|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). The whole code unit is 0x0000: the high byte must be zero. A unit whose low byte is 0x00 but whose high byte is 0x01, 0x02 or 0x03 is not a nop but the ident of a packed-switch, sparse-switch or fill-array-data payload. nop reads and writes no registers, does not touch the result register and cannot throw. Because branch offsets of 0 are illegal for goto, goto/16 and the if-* instructions, a nop can serve as a distinct target when building a tight loop.
opcodes.example:
.method public static spacer()V
    .locals 0
    nop
    return-void
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The nop has no effect; execution continues with return-void. When smali (dexlib2) assembles a method, it inserts or removes a padding nop automatically in front of payload tables that would otherwise start at an odd code-unit offset.
opcodes.registerUsage: None. nop has no operands and does not read or write any register.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Deleting a nop that sits right before a :pswitch_data / :array_ label in hand-edited smali and then worrying about alignment: smali re-pads payloads itself, so the nop is not something you must maintain by hand.
Assuming every code unit with a 0x00 low byte is a nop: 0x0100, 0x0200 and 0x0300 are payload idents, and decoders must treat them as data.
Replacing an instruction with nops to 'patch it out' without checking that later code doesn't rely on the registers it wrote or on a move-result that must immediately follow an invoke.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: move

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): destination register, v0–v15.

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): source register, v0–v15.

opcodes.summary: Copy a 32-bit non-object value from vB into vA.
opcodes.description: move copies a 32-bit non-object value (int, float, boolean, byte, char or short) from one register to another; the source is left unchanged. Use it only for primitive 32-bit values: references and wide values have their own move variants. This compact form addresses only the first 16 registers.
opcodes.technical: Format 12x (B|A|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Copies a 32-bit non-object value (int, float, boolean, byte, char or short) from vB to vA. Both registers must be in v0–v15. The verifier requires the source to hold a category-1 primitive; using it on a reference or on half of a long/double pair is rejected. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static identity(I)I
    .locals 1
    move v0, p0
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The parameter arrives in p0 and move copies it into the local register v0, which is then returned. With .locals 1 the parameter register p0 is v1, still low enough for the 4-bit fields of format 12x.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vA, reads vB. Both registers must be in v0–v15. Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Copying an object reference with plain move: references must use move-object, otherwise the verifier rejects the method.
Copying a long or double with move: only one half of the pair is copied and the verifier rejects it; use move-wide.
Naming a register above v15 (including a pN that maps above v15): smali refuses the 12x form; use move/from16 or move/16 instead.

opcodes.name: move/from16

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255.

operands.name: vBBBB
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): source register, v0–v65535.

opcodes.summary: Copy a 32-bit non-object value from vBBBB into vAA.
opcodes.description: move/from16 copies a 32-bit non-object value (int, float, boolean, byte, char or short) from one register to another; the source is left unchanged. Use it only for primitive 32-bit values: references and wide values have their own move variants. The /from16 variant lets you read from any register, which is useful for pulling values out of high registers.
opcodes.technical: Format 22x (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). Copies a 32-bit non-object value (int, float, boolean, byte, char or short) from vBBBB to vAA. The destination must be in v0–v255; the source may be any register up to v65535. The verifier requires the source to hold a category-1 primitive; using it on a reference or on half of a long/double pair is rejected. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
# v300 lives above v255, so it can only be read by /from16 or /16 moves
move/from16 v0, v300
opcodes.exampleExplanation: Most instructions can only address low registers. move/from16 brings the value from the high register v300 down into v0 so that ordinary instructions can work on it.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA, reads vBBBB. The destination must be in v0–v255; the source may be any register up to v65535.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Copying an object reference with plain move: references must use move-object, otherwise the verifier rejects the method.
Copying a long or double with move: only one half of the pair is copied and the verifier rejects it; use move-wide.
Choosing the wide-reach form when both registers are low: it works but wastes code units; smali does not shrink it for you.

operands.name: vAAAA
operands.description: AAAA (16 bits): destination register, v0–v65535.

operands.name: vBBBB
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): source register, v0–v65535.

opcodes.summary: Copy a 32-bit non-object value from vBBBB into vAAAA.
opcodes.description: move/16 copies a 32-bit non-object value (int, float, boolean, byte, char or short) from one register to another; the source is left unchanged. opcodes.name: move-wide

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): destination register pair, v0–v15 (the pair is vN, vN+1).

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): source register pair, v0–v15.

opcodes.summary: Copy a 64-bit long or double pair from vB into vA.
opcodes.description: move-wide copies a 64-bit long or double stored in a register pair from one register to another; the source is left unchanged. A long or double occupies two adjacent registers, and the instruction names only the first (lower) one of each pair. This compact form addresses only the first 16 registers.
opcodes.technical: Format 12x (B|A|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Copies a 64-bit long or double stored in a register pair from vB to vA. Both registers must be in v0–v15. Both halves of the source pair are read before anything is written, so overlapping pairs such as move-wide v1, v0 (vN to vN+1) or v0, v1 (vN to vN-1) are legal. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static identity(J)J
    .locals 2
    move-wide v0, p0
    return-wide v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The parameter arrives in p0/p1 and move-wide copies it into the local pair v0/v1, which is then returned. With .locals 2 the parameter register p0 is v2, still low enough for the 4-bit fields of format 12x.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vA/vA+1, reads vB/vB+1. Both registers must be in v0–v15. Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Naming the second half of a pair (for example v1 of v0/v1) as the source or destination, which splits a different pair and corrupts both values.
Forgetting that the destination pair also overwrites vA+1, clobbering whatever was stored in the next register.
Naming a register above v15 (including a pN that maps above v15): smali refuses the 12x form; use move-wide/from16 or move-wide/16 instead.

opcodes.name: move-object

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): destination register, v0–v15.

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): source register, v0–v15.

opcodes.summary: Copy an object reference from vB into vA.
opcodes.description: move-object copies an object reference (or null) from one register to another; the source is left unchanged. Only the reference is copied, never the object itself. This compact form addresses only the first 16 registers.
opcodes.technical: Format 12x (B|A|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Copies an object reference (or null) from vB to vA. Both registers must be in v0–v15. The verifier requires the source to hold a reference (or the null constant). Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static identity(Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object;
    .locals 1
    move-object v0, p0
    return-object v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The parameter arrives in p0 and move-object copies it into the local register v0, which is then returned. With .locals 1 the parameter register p0 is v1, still low enough for the 4-bit fields of format 12x.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vA, reads vB. Both registers must be in v0–v15. Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.

commonMistakes: Using move-object on an int or float register: the verifier expects a reference and rejects the method.

Naming a register above v15 (including a pN that maps above v15): smali refuses the 12x form; use move-object/from16 or move-object/16 instead.

opcodes.name: move-result

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255; receives the 32-bit primitive result.

opcodes.summary: Store the 32-bit primitive result of the preceding invoke in vAA.
opcodes.description: After a method call returns an int, float, boolean, byte, char or short, move-result copies that value into a register. It must be the very next instruction after the invoke; if the result is not needed, the move-result is simply omitted.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Reads the hidden result register filled by the immediately preceding invoke-kind (including invoke-polymorphic and invoke-custom) and writes it to vAA. Placing it anywhere else (after any other instruction, or after a call returning void, long, double or an object) is a verification error. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static nameLength(Ljava/lang/String;)I
    .locals 1
    invoke-virtual {p0}, Ljava/lang/String;->length()I
    move-result v0
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: String.length() returns an int, so the result is retrieved with move-result directly after the invoke-virtual and then returned.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255). Reads only the implicit result of the previous invoke.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Putting any instruction (even a const or a debug-line-only edit that adds code) between the invoke and move-result: the result is lost and the verifier rejects the method.
Using move-result for a long/double result (needs move-result-wide) or an object result (needs move-result-object).
Adding move-result after a void method call, which has no result to move.

opcodes.name: move-result-wide

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): first register of the destination pair, v0–v255; the pair is vAA, vAA+1.

opcodes.summary: Store the 64-bit (long or double) result of the preceding invoke in the pair vAA/vAA+1.
opcodes.description: Methods that return long or double hand back a 64-bit value, and move-result-wide stores it in two adjacent registers. Like the other move-result forms it has to come immediately after the invoke.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Writes both vAA and vAA+1 from the double-word result of the immediately preceding invoke-kind. Valid only directly after an invoke whose return type is J or D. The register vAA+1 must exist in the frame. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static now()J
    .locals 2
    invoke-static {}, Ljava/lang/System;->currentTimeMillis()J
    move-result-wide v0
    return-wide v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: currentTimeMillis() returns a long, which lands in the pair v0/v1. That is why the method declares .locals 2 and returns with return-wide v0.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes the pair vAA and vAA+1 (vAA in v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Reserving only one register for the result: vAA+1 is overwritten too.
Using move-result instead of move-result-wide after a call returning long or double.
Later reading vAA+1 on its own as if it were an independent int.

opcodes.name: move-result-object

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255; receives the object reference.

opcodes.summary: Store the object result of the preceding invoke or filled-new-array in vAA.
opcodes.description: When a call returns an object (including strings and arrays), move-result-object puts the reference into a register. It is also how you collect the array created by filled-new-array or filled-new-array/range. It has to be the instruction right after the producer.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Copies the reference result of the immediately preceding invoke-kind, filled-new-array or filled-new-array/range into vAA. Anywhere else it is invalid. The verifier types vAA with the method's declared return type (or the array type). Cannot throw.
opcodes.exampleExplanation: toString() returns a String reference, so move-result-object stores it in v0 for the return.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using move-result for an object-returning call: the verifier rejects the type mismatch.
Forgetting move-result-object after filled-new-array, which leaves the new array unreachable.
Separating the invoke and move-result-object when injecting logging code: put the new code after the move-result-object, not between them.

opcodes.name: move-exception

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255; receives the caught Throwable.

opcodes.summary: Store the just-caught exception in vAA; first instruction of a catch handler.
opcodes.description: When a try block throws and control jumps to a matching .catch handler, move-exception retrieves the exception object. It may only appear as the first instruction of a handler. Handlers that do not care about the exception object can simply leave it out.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Valid only as the first instruction of an exception handler (a target listed in the method's encoded_catch_handler data, written in smali with .catch/.catchall). The verifier types vAA as the caught class, or as the common superclass when one handler serves several catch types, or as Throwable for .catchall. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static parseOr(Ljava/lang/String;)I
    .locals 1
    :try_start_0
    invoke-static {p0}, Ljava/lang/Integer;->parseInt(Ljava/lang/String;)I
    move-result v0
    :try_end_0
    .catch Ljava/lang/NumberFormatException; {:try_start_0 .. :try_end_0} :catch_0
    return v0

    :catch_0
    move-exception v0
    const/4 v0, -0x1
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: If parseInt throws NumberFormatException, control continues at :catch_0, where move-exception stores the exception in v0. The handler then overwrites v0 with -1 and returns it.
opcodes.javaEquivalent: try { return Integer.parseInt(s); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { return -1; }
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Placing move-exception anywhere other than the first instruction of a handler: the verifier rejects it.
Jumping to a handler label from normal code (goto :catch_0), which makes move-exception reachable without an exception.
Forgetting that the try range in .catch is exclusive at :try_end, so the faulting instruction must come before the end label.

opcodes.name: return-void
opcodes.summary: Return from a method whose return type is void.
opcodes.description: return-void ends the current method without a value and hands control back to the caller. Every void method and every constructor (<init>) and static initializer (<clinit>) must end each path with it or with a throw.
opcodes.technical: Format 10x (ØØ|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Valid only in methods declared with return type V. Execution must never fall off the end of a method's code, so the verifier requires every path to end in a return or throw. A return does not release monitors taken with monitor-enter (dex code has no implicit method lock), so synchronized code must run monitor-exit first.
opcodes.example:
.method public constructor <init>()V
    .locals 0
    invoke-direct {p0}, Ljava/lang/Object;-><init>()V
    return-void
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: A default constructor calls the superclass constructor and then returns with return-void.
opcodes.registerUsage: None.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using return-void in a method whose descriptor returns a value: the verifier rejects it.
Deleting the final return-void while patching, so execution would fall off the end of the code.
Forgetting that constructors are void (<init>(...)V) even though new-expressions produce an object.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: return

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): return value register, v0–v255.

opcodes.summary: Return a 32-bit primitive value (int, float, boolean, ...) from the method.
opcodes.description: return ends the method and hands a 32-bit primitive value (int, float, boolean, byte, char or short) back to the caller. The caller retrieves it with move-result right after its invoke. The register's type must match the return type in the method descriptor.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Reads vAA. Valid only in methods whose return type is Z, B, S, C, I or F. A return does not release monitors taken with monitor-enter, so synchronized code must run monitor-exit first.
opcodes.example:
.method public static isEven(I)Z
    .locals 1
    rem-int/lit8 v0, p0, 0x2
    if-nez v0, :odd
    const/4 v0, 0x1
    return v0
    :odd
    const/4 v0, 0x0
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: isEven returns a boolean, which is a 32-bit value in a register, so both paths end with return v0 after loading 1 (true) or 0 (false).
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (vAA in v0–v255). Writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Returning an object with return instead of return-object, or a long with return instead of return-wide.
Returning a value from a void method: use return-void there.
Returning an int register from a method declared to return float (or vice versa) after editing the descriptor: the verifier checks the register type against the return type.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: return-wide

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): first register of the pair holding the result, v0–v255; the pair is vAA, vAA+1.

opcodes.summary: Return a 64-bit long or double held in the pair vAA/vAA+1.
opcodes.description: return-wide ends the method and hands a 64-bit long or double held in a register pair back to the caller. The caller retrieves it with move-result-wide right after its invoke. The register's type must match the return type in the method descriptor.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Reads vAA and vAA+1. Valid only in methods whose return type is J or D. A return does not release monitors taken with monitor-enter, so synchronized code must run monitor-exit first.
opcodes.example:
.method public static twice(J)J
    .locals 2
    add-long v0, p0, p0
    return-wide v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The long sum is built in the pair v0/v1, and return-wide names the first register of the pair.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA and vAA+1 (vAA in v0–v255). Writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Naming the second register of the pair (v1 for the pair v0/v1).
Using return for a long or double result: it would return only one half.
Returning a pair that was built from two unrelated int registers: the verifier tracks wide halves and rejects it.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: return-object

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the returned reference, v0–v255.

opcodes.summary: Return an object reference (or null) from the method.
opcodes.description: return-object ends the method and hands an object reference (or null) back to the caller. The caller retrieves it with move-result-object right after its invoke. The register's type must match the return type in the method descriptor.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Reads vAA. Valid only in methods whose return type is a reference type (class or array); the value must be assignable to it. A return does not release monitors taken with monitor-enter, so synchronized code must run monitor-exit first.
opcodes.example:
.method public static orEmpty(Ljava/lang/String;)Ljava/lang/String;
    .locals 0
    if-nez p0, :done
    const-string p0, ""
    :done
    return-object p0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: If the parameter is non-null it is returned unchanged; otherwise p0 is overwritten with the empty string and returned.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (vAA in v0–v255). Writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Returning a primitive register with return-object.
Returning an object whose verified type is not assignable to the declared return type: add a check-cast first.
Assuming null needs special handling: const/4 vX, 0x0 is the null reference and can be returned with return-object.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const/4

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): destination register, v0–v15.

operands.name: lit4
operands.description: B (4 bits): signed literal, -8..7 (smali: 0x0..0x7 or -0x1..-0x8); sign-extended to 32 bits.

opcodes.summary: Load a small signed literal (-8..7) into vA.
opcodes.description: const/4 is the most compact way to load a small number into a register: the whole instruction is a single code unit. It is the usual way to load 0, 1, true, false and null, because null, false and 0 all have the same bit pattern.
opcodes.technical: Format 11n (B|A|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). The 4-bit field B is sign-extended to 32 bits, so the bit pattern 0xf loads -1. The register gets the value 'as bits': the verifier decides later whether it is used as an int, float, boolean or, for 0, a null reference. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public isEnabled()Z
    .locals 1
    const/4 v0, 0x1
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The method returns true; booleans are just the ints 0 and 1 in registers, so const/4 v0, 0x1 loads true.
opcodes.javaEquivalent: boolean enabled = true;   // also: int x = 5; Object o = null;
opcodes.kotlinEquivalent: val enabled = true   // also: val x = 5; val o: Any? = null
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vA (v0–v15). Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using a value outside -8..7 (for example 0x8): smali rejects the literal; use const/16 instead.
Loading a float with const/4: 0x1 as float bits is the tiny denormal 1.4E-45, not 1.0f. Use the float bit pattern (1.0f is 0x3f800000, loaded with const/high16).
Targeting a register above v15 (or a pN that maps above v15); use const/16 there.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const/16

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255.

operands.name: lit16
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): signed literal, -32768..32767; sign-extended to 32 bits.

opcodes.summary: Load a signed 16-bit literal (-32768..32767) into vAA.
opcodes.description: const/16 loads integers that do not fit in const/4 but fit in 16 signed bits, such as 1000 or -200. It can also address registers up to v255.
opcodes.technical: Format 21s (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). The 16-bit literal BBBB is sign-extended to 32 bits (0xffff loads -1). As with every const, the register receives raw bits whose type (int or float) is decided by how they are used. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static timeoutMs()I
    .locals 1
    const/16 v0, 0x3e8    # 1000
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: 1000 is too large for const/4 but fits in 16 signed bits, so const/16 is the shortest choice.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Expecting const/16 to load 0xffff as 65535: the literal is signed, so it is -1. Use const for 65535.
Using const/16 for values like 0x10000 or larger: use const (or const/high16 when the low 16 bits are 0).
Using const/16 to fill a long register: use const-wide/16 so that both halves of the pair are written.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255.

operands.name: lit32
operands.description: BBBBBBBB (32 bits): arbitrary 32-bit constant (int bits or float bits).

opcodes.summary: Load an arbitrary 32-bit constant (int or float bits) into vAA.
opcodes.description: const loads any 32-bit value, so it is used for large ints and for float constants that no shorter form can express. Resource IDs such as 0x7f0b0012 are a common sight in decompiled apps.
opcodes.technical: Format 31i (AA|op BBBBlo BBBBhi): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). The literal is stored as two code units (low half first) and copied unchanged into vAA. smali also accepts float literals such as 1.5f and writes their IEEE 754 bits. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static maxValue()I
    .locals 1
    const v0, 0x7fffffff    # Integer.MAX_VALUE
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: Integer.MAX_VALUE needs all 32 bits, so neither const/4 nor const/16 can load it.
opcodes.javaEquivalent: int max = Integer.MAX_VALUE;   // or: float f = 1.5f;
opcodes.kotlinEquivalent: val max = Int.MAX_VALUE   // or: val f = 1.5f
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using const for a long value: it only writes one register. Use const-wide/32 or const-wide.
Assuming a resource ID loaded with const is stable across builds: aapt can renumber IDs when resources change, so patched smali must use the ID from the same build's R class / public.xml.
Choosing const when const/high16 would do (low 16 bits zero): both work, const just costs one code unit more.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const/high16

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255.

operands.name: 0xBBBB0000
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): the high 16 bits of the value; the low 16 bits are zero. In smali you write the full 32-bit value, e.g. 0x3f800000.

opcodes.summary: Load a 32-bit value whose low 16 bits are zero (e.g. 1.0f) into vAA.
opcodes.description: const/high16 stores only the upper half of a 32-bit value and fills the lower half with zeros. Many common float constants (1.0f, 2.0f, 0.5f, -1.0f) and some masks have that shape, so they fit this two-unit instruction instead of the three-unit const.
opcodes.technical: Format 21h (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). vAA = BBBB << 16 (right-zero-extended to 32 bits). In smali the operand is written as the complete value; the assembler rejects values whose low 16 bits are not zero. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static scale()F
    .locals 1
    const/high16 v0, 0x3f800000    # 1.0f
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: 1.0f has the IEEE 754 bit pattern 0x3f800000, whose low 16 bits are zero, so const/high16 can load it.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Writing only the high half in smali (const/high16 v0, 0x3f80): smali expects the full value 0x3f800000.
Using it for a value with non-zero low bits such as 1.1f (0x3f8ccccd): use const.
Confusing it with const-wide/high16, which fills a 64-bit pair (used for double constants).

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const-wide/16

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): first register of the destination pair, v0–v255; the pair is vAA, vAA+1.

operands.name: lit16
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): signed literal, -32768..32767; sign-extended to 64 bits.

opcodes.summary: Load a signed 16-bit literal, sign-extended to 64 bits, into the pair vAA/vAA+1.
opcodes.description: const-wide/16 loads a small long value such as 0L or 1000L into a register pair. It is the usual way to initialise long counters and timeouts.
opcodes.technical: Format 21s (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). The 16-bit literal is sign-extended to 64 bits and written to vAA (low word) and vAA+1 (high word). smali accepts 0x3e8 or 0x3e8L. The bits can also be used as a double, but small integers are rarely useful double bit patterns. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static defaultTimeout()J
    .locals 2
    const-wide/16 v0, 0x3e8    # 1000L
    return-wide v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The long 1000L is placed in the pair v0/v1, which is why .locals is 2.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes the pair vAA and vAA+1 (vAA in v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using const/16 for a long: only one register is written and the verifier rejects the later wide use.
Loading 1.0 (double) with const-wide/16 v0, 0x1: that is the bit pattern of a tiny denormal. Use const-wide/high16 v0, 0x3ff0000000000000L.
Forgetting that vAA+1 is overwritten as well.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const-wide/32

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): first register of the destination pair, v0–v255.

operands.name: lit32
operands.description: BBBBBBBB (32 bits): signed 32-bit literal; sign-extended to 64 bits.

opcodes.summary: Load a signed 32-bit literal, sign-extended to 64 bits, into the pair vAA/vAA+1.
opcodes.description: const-wide/32 loads long values that fit in a signed 32-bit int, for example 86400000L milliseconds in a day. Larger longs need const-wide.
opcodes.technical: Format 31i (AA|op BBBBlo BBBBhi): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). The 32-bit literal is sign-extended to 64 bits, so 0xffffffff loads -1L, not 4294967295L. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static dayMillis()J
    .locals 2
    const-wide/32 v0, 0x5265c00    # 86400000L
    return-wide v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: 86,400,000 does not fit in 16 bits but fits in 32, so const-wide/32 is the shortest encoding.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes the pair vAA and vAA+1 (vAA in v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Expecting 0xffffffff to load 4294967295L: the literal is sign-extended, giving -1L; use const-wide.
Using const (32-bit) for a long: only one register of the pair is set.
Using it for doubles: most double constants need const-wide or const-wide/high16.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const-wide

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): first register of the destination pair, v0–v255.

operands.name: lit64
operands.description: BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB (64 bits): arbitrary 64-bit constant (long bits or double bits); smali writes it with an L suffix, e.g. 0x400921fb54442d18L.

opcodes.summary: Load an arbitrary 64-bit constant (long or double) into the pair vAA/vAA+1.
opcodes.description: const-wide can load any 64-bit value, which makes it the general way to load large longs and double constants such as Math.PI. It is the only Dalvik instruction that takes five code units.
opcodes.technical: Format 51l (AA|op BBBBlo BBBB BBBB BBBBhi): 5 16-bit code units (10 bytes). The 64-bit literal is stored in four code units, least significant first, and copied unchanged into vAA (low word) and vAA+1 (high word). smali also accepts double literals such as 3.14159 and writes their IEEE 754 bits. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static pi()D
    .locals 2
    const-wide v0, 0x400921fb54442d18L    # Math.PI
    return-wide v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: Math.PI's bit pattern uses all 64 bits, so only const-wide can load it.
opcodes.javaEquivalent: double pi = Math.PI;   // or: long big = 0x123456789L;
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes the pair vAA and vAA+1 (vAA in v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Writing a long literal without the L suffix when it does not fit in an int: smali parses it as an int literal and fails; write 0x123456789L.
Reaching for const-wide when a shorter form fits: smali does not shrink const-wide for you.
Forgetting that the pair needs two registers inside .locals/.registers.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const-wide/high16

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): first register of the destination pair, v0–v255.

operands.name: 0xBBBB000000000000L
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): the top 16 bits of the 64-bit value; all lower 48 bits are zero. smali takes the full value, e.g. 0x3ff0000000000000L.

opcodes.summary: Load a 64-bit value whose low 48 bits are zero (e.g. 1.0 as double) into vAA/vAA+1.
opcodes.description: const-wide/high16 is the compact way to load 64-bit values that only use their top 16 bits. Simple double constants like 1.0, 2.0, 0.5 and -1.0 have that shape, so this is what compilers emit for them.
opcodes.technical: Format 21h (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). The pair receives BBBB << 48 (right-zero-extended to 64 bits). The smali operand is the full 64-bit value; the assembler rejects values with any of the low 48 bits set. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static one()D
    .locals 2
    const-wide/high16 v0, 0x3ff0000000000000L    # 1.0
    return-wide v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The double 1.0 is 0x3ff0000000000000, so its top 16 bits (0x3ff0) are enough to encode it.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes the pair vAA and vAA+1 (vAA in v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Writing only the top 16 bits (0x3ff0) in smali: the operand must be the full 64-bit value.
Using it for 1.1 or Math.PI (low bits non-zero): use const-wide.
Using const/high16 instead, which builds a 32-bit float, not a double pair.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const-string

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255; receives a java.lang.String reference.

operands.name: "string"
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): string_ids index (string@BBBB); smali writes the literal and the assembler assigns the index.

opcodes.summary: Load a reference to a string constant into vAA.
opcodes.description: const-string puts a reference to a string from the dex file's string pool into a register. Every string literal in Java or Kotlin source becomes a const-string (or const-string/jumbo). The same literal always yields the same interned String instance.
opcodes.technical: Format 21c (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). BBBB is an index into string_ids, so it can only reach the first 65,536 strings of the dex file; strings with larger indices need const-string/jumbo. The resulting String is interned. Resolution can in principle fail with an OutOfMemoryError, but it never throws for a valid index.
opcodes.example:
.method public static tag()Ljava/lang/String;
    .locals 1
    const-string v0, "MainActivity"
    return-object v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The literal "MainActivity" lives in the string pool; const-string loads a reference to it into v0.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Escaping strings incorrectly in smali: use Java-style escapes such as \n, \" and \u00e9 inside the quotes.
Comparing two strings with if-eq: it compares references, which only happens to work for interned literals. Call String.equals instead.
Hand-writing const-string in a huge dex where the index exceeds 0xffff: the tools must use const-string/jumbo.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const-string/jumbo

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255.

operands.name: "string"
operands.description: BBBBBBBB (32 bits): 32-bit string_ids index (string@BBBBBBBB).

opcodes.summary: Load a string constant whose pool index needs 32 bits into vAA.
opcodes.description: const-string/jumbo does the same job as const-string, but its string index is 32 bits wide. Dex files with more than 65,536 strings need it for strings beyond that limit. Apart from the size of the index, the two instructions behave identically.
opcodes.technical: Format 31c (AA|op BBBBlo BBBBhi): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). The 32-bit index into string_ids is stored low half first. The behaviour is identical to const-string: an interned java.lang.String reference is written to vAA. It is one code unit longer, which matters when re-assembling: changing const-string to /jumbo shifts branch offsets, which smali recomputes for you.
opcodes.example:
# in a large dex this string's index is above 0xffff
const-string/jumbo v0, "com.acme.demo.analytics.EVENT_OPEN"
invoke-static {v0}, Lcom/acme/demo/Analytics;->log(Ljava/lang/String;)V
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The string index does not fit in 16 bits, so the compiler used the /jumbo form to load it before logging.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Assuming /jumbo means a long string: it refers to a large string index, not a long string.
Converting /jumbo back to const-string after merging dex files without checking that the index fits.
Treating jumbo strings as obfuscation: d8/R8 emit them simply because the string pool is large.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: const-class

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255; receives a java.lang.Class reference.

operands.name: Ltype;
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): type_ids index (type@BBBB): a class, array or primitive type descriptor.

opcodes.summary: Load the java.lang.Class object for a type into vAA.
opcodes.description: const-class loads the Class object of a type, which is what a Java Foo.class literal compiles to. Android code uses it all the time, for example to build an Intent for an Activity class. For a primitive descriptor such as I, the result is the primitive's class object (int.class).
opcodes.technical: Format 21c (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). Resolves the type at type@BBBB and writes the Class reference to vAA. Resolution can fail with NoClassDefFoundError if the class is missing, or IllegalAccessError if it is not accessible. Loading the Class object does not run the class's static initializer.
opcodes.exampleExplanation: const-class supplies the Class argument of the Intent constructor, exactly like SettingsActivity.class in Java.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Expecting const-class to initialise the class: static initializers run on first use (new-instance, sget, invoke-static), not when the Class object is loaded.
Using a dotted name (com.acme.demo.Foo) instead of a descriptor (Lcom/acme/demo/Foo;).
Referencing a class that is stripped by R8 in the patched build, which leads to NoClassDefFoundError at run time.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: monitor-enter

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the object whose monitor (lock) is acquired, v0–v255.

opcodes.summary: Acquire the monitor (intrinsic lock) of the object in vAA.
opcodes.description: monitor-enter takes the lock of an object, blocking while another thread holds it. It marks the start of a synchronized block, and in dex code also the start of a synchronized method's body. Each monitor-enter must be paired with a monitor-exit on every path, including the exception path.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Throws NullPointerException if vAA is null. Monitors are re-entrant: a thread may enter a monitor it already holds, and must exit it the same number of times. In dex files ACC_SYNCHRONIZED is only valid on native methods; a Java synchronized method is merely flagged ACC_DECLARED_SYNCHRONIZED (no effect on execution), so compilers wrap its body in monitor-enter/monitor-exit on this (or on the Class object for static methods).
opcodes.example:
.method public increment()V
    .locals 1
    monitor-enter p0
    :try_start_0
    iget v0, p0, Lcom/acme/demo/Counter;->count:I
    add-int/lit8 v0, v0, 0x1
    iput v0, p0, Lcom/acme/demo/Counter;->count:I
    monitor-exit p0
    :try_end_0
    .catchall {:try_start_0 .. :try_end_0} :catchall_0
    return-void

    :catchall_0
    move-exception v0
    monitor-exit p0
    throw v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: This is the shape javac/d8 produce for synchronized (this) { count++; }: the catch-all handler releases the lock and rethrows if anything inside the block throws.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (v0–v255). Writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Exiting the method on some path without monitor-exit, which leaves the lock held.
Leaving out the catch-all handler: if code inside the block throws, the monitor is never released.
Locking on a register that may be null, which throws NullPointerException.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: monitor-exit

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the object whose monitor is released, v0–v255.

opcodes.summary: Release the monitor (intrinsic lock) of the object in vAA.
opcodes.description: monitor-exit releases a lock taken by monitor-enter and marks the end of a synchronized block. Compilers emit it twice: once on the normal path and once in a catch-all handler that then rethrows the exception.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Throws NullPointerException if vAA is null and IllegalMonitorStateException if the current thread does not hold the monitor. The spec requires that if it throws, it does so as if the pc had already advanced past the instruction, so a catch-all range that covers the monitor-exit itself can safely retry the release.
opcodes.example:
.method public increment()V
    .locals 1
    monitor-enter p0
    :try_start_0
    iget v0, p0, Lcom/acme/demo/Counter;->count:I
    add-int/lit8 v0, v0, 0x1
    iput v0, p0, Lcom/acme/demo/Counter;->count:I
    monitor-exit p0
    :try_end_0
    .catchall {:try_start_0 .. :try_end_0} :catchall_0
    return-void

    :catchall_0
    move-exception v0
    monitor-exit p0
    throw v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The lock is released on the normal path just before return-void, and again in :catchall_0 before the exception is rethrown, so the monitor is released whichever way the block ends.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (v0–v255). Writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Releasing a different object than the one locked (for example after the register was overwritten): throws IllegalMonitorStateException.
Removing the monitor-exit in the handler while patching, which can leave the lock held after an exception.
Exiting more often than entering on some path.

opcodes.name: check-cast

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the reference to check, v0–v255.

operands.name: Ltype;
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): type_ids index (type@BBBB) of the target class or array type.

opcodes.summary: Throw ClassCastException unless the reference in vAA is null or an instance of the type.
opcodes.description: check-cast is a Java cast such as (TextView) view. If the object is compatible with the type, nothing visible happens and the verifier from then on treats the register as that type. Otherwise a ClassCastException is thrown. A null reference always passes.
opcodes.technical: Format 21c (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). Reads vAA; the register is not rewritten, but its verified type is narrowed to the target type. Throws ClassCastException on mismatch; class resolution can throw NoClassDefFoundError. Because vAA must be a reference, a primitive target type always fails at run time.
opcodes.exampleExplanation: findViewById returns a View; check-cast narrows it to TextView so that the verifier accepts the following setText call on v0.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (v0–v255) and refines its static type in place; writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Removing a check-cast while patching: the verifier may then reject later calls that need the narrower type.
Expecting check-cast to fail for null: null passes every check-cast.
Expecting a result register: unlike instance-of, check-cast has no destination.

opcodes.name: instance-of

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): destination register, v0–v15; receives 1 or 0.

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): register holding the reference to test, v0–v15.

operands.name: Ltype;
operands.description: CCCC (16 bits): type_ids index (type@CCCC) of the class or array type.

opcodes.summary: Set vA to 1 if the reference in vB is an instance of the type, otherwise 0.
opcodes.description: instance-of is the Java instanceof operator. It never throws ClassCastException: it just writes 1 (true) or 0 (false) into the destination register. A null reference gives 0.
opcodes.technical: Format 22c (B|A|op CCCC): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). Writes an int (boolean) 1 or 0 to vA. Both registers use 4-bit fields (v0–v15). A primitive type index always produces 0. Class resolution can throw NoClassDefFoundError; otherwise it does not throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static isText(Ljava/lang/Object;)Z
    .locals 1
    instance-of v0, p0, Ljava/lang/String;
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: v0 becomes 1 when the argument is a String and 0 otherwise (including null), and is returned as a boolean.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vA, reads vB; both must be in v0–v15. Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Assuming instance-of also narrows the type of vB for the verifier: you still need check-cast before using vB as the subtype.
Using registers above v15: move the reference into a low register first.
Expecting true for null: instance-of always yields 0 for null.

opcodes.name: array-length

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): destination register, v0–v15; receives the length as an int.

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): register holding the array reference, v0–v15.

opcodes.summary: Store the number of elements of the array in vB into vA.
opcodes.description: array-length reads the length of any array, whatever its element type. It is what the Java expression array.length compiles to, and it shows up in nearly every for loop over an array.
opcodes.technical: Format 12x (B|A|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Throws NullPointerException if vB is null. The verifier requires vB to be an array type (or null). The result is a non-negative int.
opcodes.example:
.method public static count([Ljava/lang/String;)I
    .locals 1
    array-length v0, p0
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The length of the String[] parameter is written to v0 and returned.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vA, reads vB; both in v0–v15.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Calling array-length on a register that may be null, which throws NullPointerException.
Expecting it to work on collections: List.size() is a method call (invoke-interface), not array-length.
Using a high register; the fields are only 4 bits.

opcodes.name: new-instance

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255; receives the new, uninitialised object.

operands.name: Lclass;
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): type_ids index (type@BBBB) of a non-array class.

opcodes.summary: Allocate a new, not yet constructed instance of a class into vAA.
opcodes.description: new-instance allocates memory for an object but does not run any constructor. It is always followed by an invoke-direct of one of the class's <init> methods on the same register. Together, the two instructions form a Java new expression.
opcodes.technical: Format 21c (AA|op BBBB): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). The type must be a non-array class. Until <init> is invoked on the register, the verifier treats it as an uninitialised reference that can't be stored, passed or returned. Can throw InstantiationError for interfaces and abstract classes, IllegalAccessError, NoClassDefFoundError, OutOfMemoryError, and errors from running the class's static initializer if this is the first use of the class.
opcodes.exampleExplanation: new StringBuilder() compiles to new-instance (allocation) plus invoke-direct <init> (construction). Only after the constructor call can v0 be used for append.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vAA (v0–v255).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Forgetting the invoke-direct <init> call: the verifier rejects any use of the uninitialised object.
Calling the constructor on a copy made with move-object before initialisation: initialise the register returned by new-instance itself.
Using new-instance for arrays: arrays are created with new-array or filled-new-array.

opcodes.name: new-array

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): destination register, v0–v15; receives the new array.

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): register holding the requested length (int), v0–v15.

operands.name: [type
operands.description: CCCC (16 bits): type_ids index (type@CCCC) of an array type, e.g. [I or [Ljava/lang/String;.

opcodes.summary: Create a new array of the given array type with vB elements and store it in vA.
opcodes.description: new-array creates an array whose length comes from a register. Every element starts at its default value: 0, false, 0.0 or null. It is what new int[n] or arrayOfNulls<String>(n) compiles to.
opcodes.technical: Format 22c (B|A|op CCCC): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). The type must be an array type. Throws NegativeArraySizeException if the length is negative, OutOfMemoryError if it cannot be allocated, and resolution errors for a missing element class. For multi-dimensional types such as [[I it creates only the outer array, with null elements.
opcodes.example:
.method public static buffer(I)[B
    .locals 1
    new-array v0, p0, [B
    return-object v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: A byte[] of length p0 is allocated; all elements are 0.
opcodes.registerUsage: Writes vA, reads vB; both in v0–v15 (vA and vB may be the same register).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Passing a non-array type such as I instead of [I.
Forgetting that a negative length throws NegativeArraySizeException at run time.
Expecting new-array [[I to allocate the inner arrays too: only the outer array is created.

opcodes.name: filled-new-array

operands.name: A
operands.description: A (4 bits): array size and argument word count, 0–5; smali derives it from the register list.

operands.name: vC
operands.description: C (4 bits): first element value.

operands.name: vD
operands.description: D (4 bits): second element value.

operands.name: vE
operands.description: E (4 bits): third element value.

operands.name: vF
operands.description: F (4 bits): fourth element value.

operands.name: vG
operands.description: G (4 bits): fifth element value.

operands.name: [type
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): type_ids index (type@BBBB) of an array type with single-word elements.

opcodes.summary: Create an array from up to five registers; collect it with move-result-object.
opcodes.description: filled-new-array builds a small array directly from register values. The array is not written to a register: like a method call, it becomes the pending result and is picked up with move-result-object. Elements must be single-word values (ints or references), not long or double.
opcodes.technical: Format 35c (A|G|op BBBB F|E|D|C): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). A gives the number of elements (0–5), taken from vC..vG in order; each register field is 4 bits (v0–v15). The type must be an array type whose elements fit in one register: arrays of long or double are not allowed. Can throw OutOfMemoryError and type resolution errors.
opcodes.example:
const/4 v0, 0x1
const/4 v1, 0x2
const/4 v2, 0x3
filled-new-array {v0, v1, v2}, [I
move-result-object v3
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The three ints become the new int[]{1, 2, 3}, which move-result-object stores in v3.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vC..vG (only the first A of them), each in v0–v15; writes no register directly. The result goes to the pending result, read by move-result-object.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Forgetting move-result-object right after the instruction, which loses the array.
Trying to build a long[] or double[]: not allowed. Use new-array plus fill-array-data or aput-wide.
Listing more than five registers: use filled-new-array/range.

references.title: Dalvik bytecode: summary of bytecode set

opcodes.name: filled-new-array/range

operands.name: AA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): array size and argument word count, 0–255; smali derives it from the range.

operands.name: vCCCC
operands.description: CCCC (16 bits): first register of the consecutive range, v0–v65535.

operands.name: vNNNN
operands.description: Not encoded: last register of the range, NNNN = CCCC + AA - 1.

operands.name: [type
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): type_ids index (type@BBBB) of an array type with single-word elements.

opcodes.summary: Create an array from a consecutive register range; collect it with move-result-object.
opcodes.description: filled-new-array/range works like filled-new-array, but takes its elements from a run of consecutive registers. That removes the five-element limit and lets the elements live in high registers.
opcodes.technical: Format 3rc (AA|op BBBB CCCC): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). Elements come from vCCCC through vCCCC+AA-1, in order. The same restrictions as filled-new-array apply: array type only, no long/double elements. The result must be collected with move-result-object. Can throw OutOfMemoryError and type resolution errors.
opcodes.exampleExplanation: Six strings exceed the five-register limit, so the range form gathers v0 to v5 into a new String[].
opcodes.javaEquivalent: String[] parts = {a, b, c, d, e, f};
opcodes.kotlinEquivalent: val parts = arrayOf(a, b, c, d, e, f)
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vCCCC..vNNNN (consecutive); writes no register directly (pending result).
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using registers that are not consecutive: the range syntax only names the first and last register.
Writing {v0 .. v5} when the values are actually spread over other registers: move them into place first.
Forgetting move-result-object.

opcodes.name: fill-array-data

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the primitive array to fill, v0–v255.

operands.name: :array_data
operands.description: BBBBBBBB (32 bits): signed offset, in code units relative to this instruction, of a fill-array-data-payload; smali uses a label.

opcodes.summary: Copy constant data from a fill-array-data-payload table into the array in vAA.
opcodes.description: fill-array-data copies a block of constant values into an existing primitive array in one step. Compilers use it for array initialisers such as {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}, after allocating the array with new-array. The values themselves sit in a payload table, usually at the end of the method.
opcodes.technical: Format 31t (AA|op BBBBlo BBBBhi): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). The offset points to a fill-array-data-payload (ident 0x0300) that must be 4-byte aligned. The array must be an array of primitives whose element width matches the payload's element_width. The table may be shorter than the array, in which case only the first elements are set; it must not be longer (ART throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException). Throws NullPointerException if vAA is null. The payload's size in code units is (size * element_width + 1) / 2 + 4.
opcodes.example:
.method public static primes()[I
    .locals 1
    const/4 v0, 0x5
    new-array v0, v0, [I
    fill-array-data v0, :array_0
    return-object v0

    :array_0
    .array-data 4
        0x2
        0x3
        0x5
        0x7
        0xb
    .end array-data
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: A 5-element int[] is allocated and then filled from the .array-data table (element width 4 bytes). smali turns the .array-data block into a fill-array-data-payload and pads it to an even code-unit offset.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (the array reference, v0–v255); writes the array's elements in memory, no registers.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using it on an object array (String[]): only primitive arrays are allowed.
Declaring the wrong width in .array-data (for example 4 for a byte[]): the width must match the element type (1 for byte/boolean, 2 for short/char, 4 for int/float, 8 for long/double).
Putting more elements in the table than the array holds.

opcodes.name: throw

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the Throwable to throw, v0–v255.

opcodes.summary: Throw the exception object held in vAA.
opcodes.description: throw raises the exception object in a register. Control passes to the nearest matching catch handler in this method or further up the call stack. The exception is usually created just before with new-instance and an <init> call.
opcodes.technical: Format 11x (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). vAA must hold a reference to a java.lang.Throwable (or a subclass). If vAA is null, a NullPointerException is thrown instead. Like return, throw ends the current path, so no fall-through instruction is needed after it.
opcodes.example:
new-instance v0, Ljava/lang/IllegalArgumentException;
const-string v1, "count < 0"
invoke-direct {v0, v1}, Ljava/lang/IllegalArgumentException;-><init>(Ljava/lang/String;)V
throw v0
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The exception is allocated, constructed with a message and then thrown with throw v0.
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (v0–v255). Writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Throwing a register that does not hold a Throwable: the verifier rejects it.
Throwing the object before calling its constructor (an uninitialised reference).
Expecting code after throw to run: the path ends at the throw.

opcodes.name: goto

operands.name: :label
operands.description: AA (8 bits): signed branch offset in 16-bit code units relative to the start of this instruction (-128..127); smali uses a label.

opcodes.summary: Unconditionally jump by a signed 8-bit code-unit offset.
opcodes.description: goto always transfers control to the target instruction. Compilers use it to close loops and to jump over else-branches. The 8-bit offset reaches 128 code units backwards or 127 forwards, enough for short loops.
opcodes.technical: Format 10t (AA|op): 1 16-bit code unit (2 bytes). Target = address of this instruction + AA (signed, in code units). The offset must not be 0; a loop that branches to itself has to use goto/32 or a nop as target. The target must be the start of an instruction inside the same method. Cannot throw. When assembling, smali/dexlib2 automatically widens goto to goto/16 or goto/32 if the computed offset does not fit.
opcodes.example:
.method public static sumTo(I)I
    .locals 2
    const/4 v0, 0x0    # sum
    const/4 v1, 0x0    # i
    :loop
    if-gt v1, p0, :done
    add-int/2addr v0, v1
    add-int/lit8 v1, v1, 0x1
    goto :loop
    :done
    return v0
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: goto :loop jumps back a few code units to the loop condition, well within the 8-bit range. smali computes the offset from the label.
opcodes.javaEquivalent: while (...) { ... }   // or: break / continue / the jump over an else-branch
opcodes.registerUsage: None.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Jumping into the middle of a try range or between an invoke and its move-result, which breaks the verifier's assumptions.
Hand-computing offsets: let smali compute them from labels.
Writing goto :self (offset 0) for a spin loop with goto or goto/16: smali assembles it, but the spec forbids a zero offset for these forms, so the verifier rejects it; use goto/32.

operands.name: :label
operands.description: AAAA (16 bits): signed branch offset in 16-bit code units relative to the start of this instruction (-32768..32767); smali uses a label.

opcodes.summary: Unconditionally jump by a signed 16-bit code-unit offset.
opcodes.description: goto/16 always transfers control to the target instruction. Compilers use it to close loops and to jump over else-branches. The 16-bit offset reaches about 32 K code units in either direction.
opcodes.technical: Format 20t (ØØ|op AAAA): 2 16-bit code units (4 bytes). Target = address of this instruction + AAAA (signed, in code units). The offset must not be 0; a loop that branches to itself has to use goto/32 or a nop as target. The target must be the start of an instruction inside the same method. Cannot throw. When assembling, smali/dexlib2 automatically widens goto to goto/16 or goto/32 if the computed offset does not fit.

:loop_start
# ... a loop body larger than 127 code units ...
add-int/lit8 v1, v1, 0x1
goto/16 :loop_start
opcodes.exampleExplanation: The loop body is too large for an 8-bit offset, so the back-edge uses goto/16. If you write plain goto, smali widens it automatically when the label is out of range.
opcodes.javaEquivalent: while (...) { ... }   // or: break / continue / the jump over an else-branch
opcodes.registerUsage: None.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Jumping into the middle of a try range or between an invoke and its move-result, which breaks the verifier's assumptions.
Hand-computing offsets: let smali compute them from labels.
Writing goto :self (offset 0) for a spin loop with goto or goto/16: smali assembles it, but the spec forbids a zero offset for these forms, so the verifier rejects it; use goto/32.

opcodes.name: goto/32

operands.name: :label
operands.description: AAAAAAAA (32 bits): signed branch offset in 16-bit code units relative to the start of this instruction (the full signed 32-bit range); smali uses a label.

opcodes.summary: Unconditionally jump by a signed 32-bit code-unit offset.
opcodes.description: goto/32 always transfers control to the target instruction. Compilers use it to close loops and to jump over else-branches. The 32-bit offset can reach any instruction in the method.
opcodes.technical: Format 30t (ØØ|op AAAAlo AAAAhi): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). Target = address of this instruction + AAAAAAAA (signed, in code units). Unlike goto and goto/16, the offset may be 0, so goto/32 can branch to itself (a legal spin loop). The target must be the start of an instruction inside the same method. Cannot throw. When assembling, smali/dexlib2 automatically widens goto to goto/16 or goto/32 if the computed offset does not fit.
opcodes.example:
# in a huge generated method the target is more than 32767 code units away
goto/32 :far_target
opcodes.exampleExplanation: Only goto/32 reaches targets beyond the 16-bit range. dexlib2 promotes goto and goto/16 to goto/32 when needed.
opcodes.javaEquivalent: while (...) { ... }   // or: break / continue / the jump over an else-branch
opcodes.registerUsage: None.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Jumping into the middle of a try range or between an invoke and its move-result, which breaks the verifier's assumptions.
Hand-computing offsets: let smali compute them from labels.
Using goto/32 everywhere 'to be safe': it works but costs three code units per jump.

opcodes.name: packed-switch

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the int value to switch on, v0–v255.

operands.name: :pswitch_data
operands.description: BBBBBBBB (32 bits): signed offset, in code units relative to this instruction, of a packed-switch-payload; smali uses a label.

opcodes.summary: Jump through a table of consecutive int cases, or fall through if the value is out of range.
opcodes.description: packed-switch is the jump table for a switch whose case values are consecutive, such as 0, 1, 2, 3. The value selects an entry directly by its distance from the first key, so dispatch takes constant time. Values outside the table fall through to the next instruction, which acts as the default branch.
opcodes.technical: Format 31t (AA|op BBBBlo BBBBhi): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). The payload (ident 0x0100) holds size, first_key and size branch targets. If first_key <= vAA < first_key + size, control goes to targets[vAA - first_key]; otherwise execution continues with the next instruction. The targets are relative to the address of the packed-switch instruction, not of the table. The payload must be 4-byte aligned and takes (size * 2) + 4 code units. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static label(I)Ljava/lang/String;
    .locals 1
    packed-switch p0, :pswitch_data_0
    const-string v0, "other"
    return-object v0

    :pswitch_0
    const-string v0, "zero"
    return-object v0

    :pswitch_1
    const-string v0, "one"
    return-object v0

    :pswitch_2
    const-string v0, "two"
    return-object v0

    :pswitch_data_0
    .packed-switch 0x0
        :pswitch_0
        :pswitch_1
        :pswitch_2
    .end packed-switch
.end method
opcodes.exampleExplanation: Values 0, 1 and 2 jump to their case labels via the table; any other value falls through to the code right after packed-switch, which returns "other" (the default branch).
opcodes.javaEquivalent: switch (n) { case 0: return "zero"; case 1: return "one"; case 2: return "two"; default: return "other"; }
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vAA (v0–v255). Writes nothing.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Pointing two switch instructions at the same payload label: dexlib2/smali refuses this; each switch needs its own table.
Forgetting that the default case is the fall-through path directly after the switch instruction.
Editing the .packed-switch first key without re-ordering the labels: entry i always belongs to the value first_key + i.

opcodes.name: sparse-switch

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): register holding the int value to switch on, v0–v255.

operands.name: :sswitch_data

    return-object v0

    const-string v0, "Not Found"
    return-object v0

    return-object v0

opcodes.name: cmpl-float

operands.name: vAA
operands.description: AA (8 bits): destination register, v0–v255; receives -1, 0 or 1 as an int.

operands.name: vBB
operands.description: BB (8 bits): first source register, v0–v255.

operands.name: vCC
operands.description: CC (8 bits): second source register, v0–v255.

opcodes.summary: Compare two floats: vAA = -1, 0 or 1; NaN gives -1 (lt bias).

opcodes.name: if-eq

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): first register to compare, v0–v15.

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): second register to compare, v0–v15.

operands.name: :label
operands.description: CCCC (16 bits): signed branch offset in code units relative to this instruction (-32768..32767, never 0); smali uses a label.

opcodes.summary: Branch to the label if vA == vB (32-bit compare).
opcodes.description: if-eq jumps to the label if the value in vA is equal to the value in vB; otherwise execution continues with the next instruction. It works on ints and also on two object references, where it checks identity (the same object), not equals(). Compilers usually emit the inverse test to skip over a block: if (a == b) {...} becomes if-ne a, b, :skip.

Long, float and double values must be compared with cmp-long/cmpl-*/cmpg-* followed by an if-*z test. The offset is in code units from the start of this instruction and must not be 0. Both register fields are 4 bits. Cannot throw.
opcodes.example:
.method public static check(II)Z
    .locals 1
    if-eq p0, p1, :yes
    const/4 v0, 0x0
    return v0
    :yes
    const/4 v0, 0x1
    return v0
.end method

opcodes.kotlinEquivalent: if (a == b) { ... }   // a === b for references
opcodes.registerUsage: Reads vA and vB (both v0–v15). Writes nothing. Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Forgetting that javac inverts conditions: the if-ne you see in decompiled code usually guards the body of if (a == b).

Using it on long/float/double registers: compare with cmp-long, cmpl-* or cmpg-* first.
Using registers above v15: move them into low registers first or use cmp + if-*z.

operands.name: vA
operands.description: A (4 bits): first register to compare, v0–v15.

operands.name: vB
operands.description: B (4 bits): second register to compare, v0–v15.

operands.name: :label
operands.description: CCCC (16 bits): signed branch offset in code units relative to this instruction (-32768..32767, never 0); smali uses a label.

opcodes.summary: Branch to the label if vA <= vB (32-bit compare).

    return v0
    :yes

    return v0
.end method

opcodes.name: invoke-virtual
opcodes.syntax: invoke-virtual {vC, vD, vE, vF, vG}, Lclass;->method(params)ret

operands.name: A
operands.description: A (4 bits): argument word count, 0–5; smali derives it from the register list.

operands.name: vC
operands.description: C (4 bits): first argument register (the receiver for instance calls).

operands.name: vD
operands.description: D (4 bits): second argument register.

operands.name: vE
operands.description: E (4 bits): third argument register.

operands.name: vF
operands.description: F (4 bits): fourth argument register.

operands.name: vG
operands.description: G (4 bits): fifth argument register.

operands.name: Lclass;->method(params)ret
operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): method_ids index (meth@BBBB).

opcodes.summary: Call a virtual method, dispatched on the receiver's runtime class.
opcodes.description: invoke-virtual calls an ordinary instance method: one that is not static, private or a constructor. The method that actually runs is chosen at run time from the receiver's class, so overrides in subclasses are honoured.
opcodes.technical: Format 35c (A|G|op BBBB F|E|D|C): 3 16-bit code units (6 bytes). At most five argument words, and every register must be in v0–v15. Argument words count this as one word and each long/double as two. The first register is the receiver (this). Dispatch uses the receiver's runtime class's vtable. Throws NullPointerException for a null receiver; resolution can throw NoSuchMethodError, IncompatibleClassChangeError (static or interface method) or IllegalAccessError; AbstractMethodError if the selected method is abstract. A return value is only available to a move-result* placed immediately after the call.

opcodes.registerUsage: Reads the listed registers (at most five, each v0–v15) as argument words, receiver first for non-static calls; a long/double argument is listed as two consecutive registers. Writes no register directly: the result, if any, is collected with move-result*. Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.
opcodes.compatibility: Original Dalvik instruction: valid in every dex version (035 and later) and on every Android release (API 1+), under both Dalvik and ART.
commonMistakes: Using invoke-virtual for a private method or constructor (use invoke-direct) or for an interface method (use invoke-interface).
Forgetting the receiver register: the first register is always this.
Listing only one register for a long/double argument: write both halves, e.g. {p1, p2} for a long in p1/p2.
Putting other code between the invoke and its move-result*.

operands.description: BBBB (16 bits): method_ids index (meth@BBBB).

The first call initialises the declaring class (its <clinit> may run and fail with ExceptionInInitializerError). Resolution can throw NoSuchMethodError, IncompatibleClassChangeError (if the method is not static) or IllegalAccessError. A return value is only available to a move-result* placed immediately after the call.

.method public static clamp(I)I
    .locals 1
    const/16 v0, 0x64
    invoke-static {p0, v0}, Ljava/lang/Math;->min(II)I

    return p0
.end method

Remember that pN registers are aliases for the last registers of the frame: in a method with many locals, p0 may be v20 or higher and then cannot be named by a 4-bit register field.

Calling an instance method with invoke-static, which fails resolution with IncompatibleClassChangeError.
Listing only one register for a long/double argument: write both halves, e.g. {p1, p2} for a long in p1/p2.
Putting other code between the invoke and its move-result*.
